<objective>
Close the two billing guarantees that live outside the spawn itself: the startup gate that refuses to
dispatch at all unless the CLI is authenticated on a subscription, and the redaction that keeps a secret
out of the event store and the logs once one appears in output Fleet did not author.

Purpose: BILL-05 is the guarantee that catches a machine whose `claude` login has expired or been
switched to an API key — a state no per-spawn check can detect, because by then the session has already
started. BILL-08 is the guarantee that a secret appearing in an agent's stdout, a setup command's output,
or a git error message does not become a permanent row in an append-only table.

Output: a startup preflight with a structured signal rather than string-scraping, a single redaction
matcher used by both persistence paths, and a test proving SAFE-06's two layers are genuinely
independent.
</objective>

  <behavior>
    - Given a stubbed `claude auth status` returning `{ loggedIn: true, authMethod: 'claude.ai', subscriptionType: 'max' }`: `verifySubscriptionAuth()` resolves to an ok result.
    - Given `{ loggedIn: true, authMethod: 'apiKey' }`: it returns a refusal naming the observed `authMethod`.
    - Given `{ loggedIn: false }`: it returns a refusal.
    - Given output that is not valid JSON, or valid JSON missing the `loggedIn` or `authMethod` key: it returns a refusal whose reason states the shape was unrecognised — never an ok result, and never a refusal that misreports the cause as "not logged in".
    - Given a non-zero exit from the `claude` binary, or the binary being absent from `PATH`: it returns a refusal rather than throwing an unhandled error.
    - `verifyPermissionModeSupported('acceptEdits')` parses `claude --help` and returns ok when the mode appears among the accepted choices, and a refusal naming the observed choice list when it does not.
    - When either preflight refuses, `startDaemon()` does not begin dispatching: the scheduler is constructed in a refusing state and `POST /tasks` responds with the `preflight_failed` error code.
  </behavior>
  <action>
Create `src/runner/preflight.ts` implementing D-07 and BILL-05. Open it with the phase's header-comment
convention: name the requirement IDs and the property it defends.

Export `verifySubscriptionAuth(deps)` which invokes `claude auth status` via an argv array with
`buildAllowlistedEnv()` as its environment, and parses stdout as JSON. RESEARCH.md verified live against
2.1.218 that JSON is the DEFAULT output format for this subcommand (`--json` is documented as the
default, `--text` is the opt-in), and that it returns
`{ loggedIn, authMethod, apiProvider, email, orgId, orgName, subscriptionType }`. This is a structured
signal — do NOT string-scrape the human-readable output.

Gate on `loggedIn === true && authMethod === 'claude.ai'`. Do NOT additionally gate on
`subscriptionType`: `authMethod` is the actual billing-mode signal (an `apiKey` value is what per-token
billing looks like), while `subscriptionType` (`max`, `pro`, and so on) is informational and gating on a
specific tier would refuse dispatch for a legitimate account.

Handle the unrecognised-shape case explicitly and deliberately. VALIDATION.md records this as a
manual-only verification precisely because the field names are an external contract Fleet does not own: a
future CLI version could rename them. The refusal must state that the shape was unrecognised. Silently
treating a missing `loggedIn` key as `false` would produce a confusing but safe outcome; silently
treating a missing `authMethod` as acceptable would produce a silent billing flip, which is the failure
mode this whole phase exists to prevent. Return a discriminated `PreflightResult`
(`{ ok: true, detail }` or `{ ok: false, code, reason, observed }`) rather than throwing, and define
`PreflightError` for the callers that want to throw.

Export `verifyPermissionModeSupported(mode)` which runs `claude --help`, extracts the accepted choice
list for `--permission-mode`, and returns a refusal when the configured mode is not among them. SPIKE-02
already demonstrated both that this parse works and that the choice list is version-dependent, which is
why this is a runtime assertion rather than a compile-time constant. This closes the Phase 1 deferred
item that explicitly said "revisit in Phase 2 alongside BILL-05" — both checks are "verify the CLI before
dispatching," so they belong at one call site.

Wire both into `startDaemon()` in `src/api/http/app.ts`, before `app.listen()`. On refusal, log the
reason at error level and construct the scheduler in a refusing state so `POST /tasks` returns the
`preflight_failed` code. `preflight_failed: 503` is ALREADY present in `CODE_TO_STATUS` — plan 02-04
added the complete code set for this phase in one pass, and `src/api/http/errors.ts` must NOT be edited
by this plan (it is owned by 02-04, and editing it here would collide with the other wave-3 plans).
Throw a `PreflightError` carrying `code: 'preflight_failed'` and let the generic code-keyed branch in
`registerErrorHandler` render it. Do NOT exit the process: the daemon must stay up and
serve `GET /tasks` and `/health` so the developer can see WHY nothing is dispatching. A daemon that
silently exits is indistinguishable from a daemon that crashed.

Create `src/runner/preflight.test.ts` covering every `<behavior>` case. Inject the command runner as a
dependency so the tests stub `claude auth status` output rather than requiring a real CLI — these must be
hermetic `unit`-project tests, not spike probes.
  </action>

    - A test builds the app with a refusing preflight and asserts `POST /tasks` responds `503` with `error.code === 'preflight_failed'`, while `GET /health` still responds `200`.

  <done>The daemon refuses to dispatch, visibly and with a stated reason, whenever it cannot positively confirm subscription authentication.</done>

  </read_first>
  <behavior>
    - `redact('REDACTED_SECRET...')` replaces the token with `REDACTION_TOKEN` and leaves surrounding text intact.
    - The same holds for a `ghp_`-prefixed token, an `AKIA`-prefixed token, and an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header line.
    - A key-name match also fires: a JSON fragment `"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY":"whatever"` has its VALUE replaced while the key name stays readable.
    - A base64-shaped run of exactly `MIN_BASE64_RUN` characters is redacted; a run of `MIN_BASE64_RUN - 1` characters is left untouched.
    - `redact('')` returns `''`; a payload with no secret-shaped value returns byte-identical output.
    - A payload with three distinct secret-shaped values has all three replaced.
    - `redact(redact(x)) === redact(x)` for every fixture input.
    - `REDACTION_TOKEN` itself does not match any pattern in `SECRET_PATTERNS`.
  </behavior>
  <action>
Create `src/core/event-store/redact.ts` exporting a pure `redact(payload: string): string`, a named
`REDACTION_TOKEN` constant, a named `MIN_BASE64_RUN` threshold constant, and the `SECRET_PATTERNS`
array. This is the single definition site for the matching rules; nothing anywhere else in the tree may
declare a competing regex.

Match on VALUE SHAPE in addition to known key names, per D-08. A secret's name in an arbitrary
repository's output is not predictable — an agent's stdout, a `.fleet.yml` setup command's stderr, or a
git error message can carry a credential under any label — so shape matching is what makes this
tractable. Cover at minimum: `sk-ant-` prefixed tokens, `ghp_`/`gho_`/`ghs_` GitHub tokens, `AKIA`
prefixed AWS access key ids, an `Authorization`/`Bearer` header value, and a long unbroken base64-charset
run. Pair that with key-name matching for the credential variable families PITFALLS.md enumerates,
replacing the value while leaving the key readable so a redacted payload still tells the reader WHICH
credential shape appeared.

Set `MIN_BASE64_RUN` conservatively — a threshold too low will redact legitimate hashes and file paths in
diffs and make the event log useless. Pick a value at or above 40 and pin the exact adjacency behavior
with a test at the threshold and one character below it, so a later tuning change is caught rather than
silently widening or narrowing the match.

Choose `REDACTION_TOKEN` so it cannot itself match any pattern — this is what makes `redact` idempotent,
and the idempotency test is what proves it. Apply every pattern globally, not first-match-only.

Create `src/core/event-store/redact.test.ts` covering every `<behavior>` case, with the base64 threshold
tests written against the exported `MIN_BASE64_RUN` constant rather than a hardcoded length, so the test
tracks the constant.
  </action>
  <verify>
    <automated>npm test -- src/core/event-store/redact.test.ts</automated>
  </verify>

    - A test asserts a payload containing three distinct secret shapes has all three replaced.
    - A test asserts `redact(redact(x))` equals `redact(x)` for every fixture input via `it.each`.
    - A test asserts `SECRET_PATTERNS.some(p => p.test(REDACTION_TOKEN))` is `false`.
    - `MIN_BASE64_RUN` is at least 40.
    - `npm test` (whole `unit` project) exits 0.
  </acceptance_criteria>
  <done>One pure, idempotent, globally-applied redaction function exists, with its threshold behavior pinned at the boundary.</done>
